lisa: Heads up — support repro'd a 400 on POST /v1/files/upload. Docs show "metadata" as an object, runtime expects an array of key/value. Customer payload: `{"file_url":"https://...","metadata":{"owner":"alice","env":"prod"}}` -> 400 
neil: Oof. Is this an OpenAPI vs runtime mismatch?
lisa: Yep. OpenAPI schema allows additionalProperties (object). Runtime marshals to S3 expecting [{key,value}].
neil: We should fix the schema to an array and add example snippets for curl/python/js/go. Also add migration guidance and a deprecation note for the object form.
docs-bot: neil opened PR #2421: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2421
zane: Recommend server accept both shapes for the next 90 days for v1 compatibility, but doc must be explicit about timeline.
neil: Adding code samples to the PR:
- curl: `{"metadata":[{"key":"owner","value":"alice"}]}`
- python helper: `if isinstance(metadata, dict): metadata = [{"key":k, "value":v} for k,v in metadata.items()]`
- js: `Object.entries(metadata||{}).map(([k,v])=>({key:k,value:v}))`
- go: `func ToKV(m map[string]string) []Metadata { ... }`
lisa: Also call out duplicate keys/ordering: object loses duplicates and ordering depends on language; array preserves them.
zane: Add a docs CI test that validates example JSON files against the OpenAPI schema so we don't regress. I'll open a follow-up in infra-docs.
neil: I'll include a short migration section and a changelog + support KB blurb. Can someone from SDKs confirm whether client libs will need changes?
lisa: Python/JS will still send dicts by default until we bump generator. Go will need a helper. We'll add snippets for all and a small generator note.
docs-bot: Merged to staging; pending docs CI and prod deploy.
